exercĭtĭum , ii, n. id.,
I.exercise (postAug.; not in Cic. and Caes.): frequentibus exercitiis praeparare milites ad proelia, Sall. Fragm. ap. Veg. Mil. 1, 9 fin.: “equitum,” Tac. A. 2, 55 ; cf. Vell. 2, 109: “aliarum quoque rerum vel studio vel exercitio eum teneri,” Gell. 3, 1, 12 : “in exercitiis disci,” i. e. plays, Vulg. 2 Macc. 4, 14 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
